data.title: Urea (10% cream; urea + lactic acid)
data.summary: VI Keratolytics & emollients · Humectant (low concentration) and keratolytic (high concentration)
data.body:
_Topicals · VI Keratolytics & emollients_

**Class:** Humectant (low concentration) and keratolytic (high concentration)

## Mechanism of action
- At 10% or less: humectant — draws water into the stratum corneum (natural moisturising factor component)
- At 20–40%: keratolytic — breaks hydrogen bonds in keratin, dissolves scale
- 40% (under occlusion): softens and dissolves dystrophic nail plate (chemical nail avulsion)
- Lactic acid (α-hydroxy acid) adds humectant and keratolytic action; the combination is better for thick scaling

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 10%: xerosis, atopic dermatitis (dry skin), mild ichthyosis, elderly dry skin
- Urea + lactic acid (e.g. urea 10–12% + lactic acid 10%): ichthyosis vulgaris, X-linked and lamellar ichthyosis, keratosis pilaris, palmoplantar keratoderma, cracked heels
- 20–40%: hyperkeratosis of soles, calluses
- 40% paste: onychomycosis/nail psoriasis nail avulsion (before topical antifungal)
- Enhances penetration of topical steroids and antifungals

## Dose & formulations
- Apply once or twice daily, ideally after bathing on damp skin

## Adverse effects
- Stinging or burning, especially on inflamed or fissured skin and in young children
- Irritation of face and mucosa

## Contraindications
- Acutely inflamed or broken skin; infants (stinging) — use with caution

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Concentration determines action: humectant (≤10%) vs keratolytic (20–40%) vs nail avulsion (40%)
- Stings on eczematous skin

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.55; Khopkar ch.27. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
